image_description: A museum exhibit featuring a large Triceratops fossil skeleton. The image focuses on the massive skull with its three horns and large frill, mounted on a quadrupedal frame. The background shows other skeletal exhibits and museum architecture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fossil clearly displays the characteristic three-horn arrangement: two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a fossil skeleton; the keratinous beak (soft tissue) is not preserved or visible, only the underlying bone structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mount shows four sturdy, vertical limbs supporting the body mass, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, shield-like bone structure at the back of the skull is clearly visible and dominates the head profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) and shows texture consistent with fossilized bone and marginal ornamentation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As a skeleton, no skin, scales, or soft tissue structures are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mounting posture shows the shoulders lower than the hips, creating the characteristic slope.
The visible portion of the tail behind the hindlimbs is thick and relatively short compared to the body length.

To ensure the complex geometry of the frill and horns is structurally coherent and not fused with the background.
